text: The Czech exiles in London used EVA (a message written into a triangle twice) and Chiffre XIII (five rows of a keyword's width, then five shifted rows of one scrambled alphabet in turn). Sanborn reportedly spaced YAR '1-2-3'.

Every key from the earlier messages' text and the dictionary, every open choice of XIII's short rows enumerated, and the YAR spacing as counting-off orders, each against the known letters and scrambled copies.
Nothing fits better than on the copies; under Chiffre XIII's substitution no mask fits K4 or any copy at all. Closed.
